correctness.rationale: For fixed 1/2<p<1 on C_n, lifted nearest-neighbor trajectory covers precisely when its range first reaches n−1. Gambler’s ruin gives ultimate minimum K geometric with tail r^k, r=(1−p)/p. Let b=floor((n−1)/2); E={K≤b, minimum through H_b equals ultimate minimum}. The probability of K>b and the chance of a lower minimum after H_b are each at most r^(b+1). On E the range cannot reach n−1 before H_(n−1−K), and at that time its last new residue is n−1−K. Therefore the dependent joint path coupling fails with probability ≤2r^(b+1). First passage increments are iid with mean 1/(2p−1), variance 4p(1−p)/(2p−1)^3; the CLT applies. Tight K makes the shifted passage-time error O_P(1). Conditional strong Markov at fixed early s and a uniform CLT over finitely many positions prove asymptotic independence of K and normalized H_(n−1); taking s→∞ gives the Gaussian–geometric product limit. No assumption of finite-n independence is used.
